[operation: meeting-list-put]



READ-ONLY



List meetings within a time range, paginated.



Returns meetings within a time range (paginated). Prefer this over the GET form: filters travel in the request body, so long workspace or status lists don't hit URL-length limits. Narrow by workspace and by status (Active, Canceled, NoShow, Completed). The window may not exceed 7 days.

→

    {results: [{meetingId, status, scheduledAt, attendees, assignedUserId, workspaceId}], pagination}

see: meetin

[operation: meeting-get]



READ-ONLY



Fetches full record for a single meeting by meetingId.

- meetingId (req): UUID

→ meeting object (payload structure may change); key fields: meetingStatus (not "status"), activities (array including a ScheduledAt entry — no top-level scheduledAt), id (not "meetingId"); no top-level linkedCrmEventIds

see: meeting-list (find meetingId by time range), meeting-cancel/noshow (change status), meeting-activity (admin URL), crm-get (if CRM ID known)

[operation: meeting-export-v2-put]



READ-ONLY



Exports meetings in a time range as CSV via v2 streaming endpoint. Accepts filter params in request body. Max window: 7 days.

- body.start, body.end (req): ISO-8601; max 7-day span

- body.workspaceIds (opt): filter by workspace

- body.assigneeIds (opt): filter by assignee user IDs (array of userId strings); use user-find to resolve email → userId

- body.hostIds (opt): filter by host user IDs (array of userId strings); use user-find to resolv

params.name: redirectOnSuccess
params.description: Redirect to this url on success

params.name: redirectOnFailure
params.description: Redirect to this url on failure

[operation: meeting-cancel]



MUTATING — DESTRUCTIVE, has external side effects



Permanently cancels meeting by meetingId; sets CANCELLED, may update calendar/CRM and trigger automations.

- meetingId (req)

→

    {}

⚠ irreversible; may email attendees

see: meeting-get (verify status before/after), crm-cancel (if CRM ID known)
